title: Locality in Dissipative Ground-State Preparation
authors: Qicheng Tang, Ruhanshi Barad, Xueda Wen
abstract: Can the ground state of a local Hamiltonian be prepared by local dissipation? We address this question for free-fermion Hamiltonians, using a quadratic Lindbladian with linear jump operators for the dissipative ground-state preparation. For translation-invariant targets, Fourier correspondence relates spatial locality to momentum-space analyticity, allowing us to derive a complete spectral criterion for the existence of exponentially local linear jump operators that prepare the ground state. This criterion leads to a no-go theorem that, sign-changing Fermi-level crossings exclude exponentially local linear jump operators for preparing the ground state. While these crossings are the complete obstruction in one dimension, additional obstructions generally arise in higher dimensions. We illustrate these additional obstructions using two quadratic-band-touching models with algebraically decaying ground-state correlations. We further show that short-range ground-state correlations, although not necessary, are sufficient for local dissipative preparation even without translation invariance. Our results establish how the spectral structure of the target Hamiltonian governs the locality of dissipative ground-state preparation.
summary: This paper establishes rigorous spectral criteria determining when the ground state of a local Hamiltonian can be prepared via local dissipation. It proves that spectral features, such as sign-changing Fermi-level crossings, act as necessary obstructions to this preparation process. The findings connect the spectral structure of the target state to the required locality of the dissipative coupling operators.
main_problem: The central question is whether the ground state of a local Hamiltonian can be prepared using local dissipation mechanisms.
main_result: The authors derive a spectral criterion showing that sign-changing Fermi-level crossings are obstructions to local preparation in 1D, and they identify additional obstructions in higher dimensions.
method: The analysis uses the Fourier correspondence for translation-invariant systems to relate spatial locality of jump operators to analyticity in momentum space, leading to spectral selection rules.
model_or_system: The study focuses on free-fermion Hamiltonians on a d-dimensional lattice, governed by a quadratic Lindbladian describing the dissipative evolution.
key_observables: Locality (exponential decay of jump operator coefficients), spectral structure (Fermi-level crossings), and the existence of a spectral criterion.
important_parameters: Dimensionality (d), the gap structure of the target Hamiltonian, and the nature of the correlations (short-range vs. algebraic).
main_assumptions: The analysis primarily focuses on free-fermion systems and assumes the use of quadratic Lindbladians with linear jump operators.
paper_structure: The paper develops the necessary and sufficient criterion for exponential locality, first establishing the no-go theorem based on Fermi-level crossings in 1D, then generalizing to higher dimensions, and finally showing sufficiency using short-range correlations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the feasibility and limitations of engineering quantum states using open system dynamics, which is crucial for understanding quantum control and thermalization processes in many-body systems.
